svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Genetic modification: making human insulin in bacteria."], [1, "A restriction enzyme cuts the insulin gene out of human DNA, leaving sticky ends."], [4, "The same enzyme cuts open a plasmid, leaving complementary sticky ends."], [7, "The gene is placed in the plasmid; sticky ends pair and DNA ligase seals the backbone: a recombinant plasmid."], [10, "Bacteria take up the plasmid. Antibiotic in the agar kills bacteria without it."], [13, "Transformed bacteria multiply and make human insulin."]]
svg.title: Recombinant DNA: insulin
svg.desc: Making human insulin in bacteria: a restriction enzyme cuts out the insulin gene and opens a plasmid, DNA ligase joins them into a recombinant plasmid, bacteria are transformed and selected with an antibiotic marker, and they produce insulin.
svg.text: Sticky ends shown with their bases. Not to scale.

g.data-info: The gene of interest, cut out with a restriction enzyme.
Cuts DNA at a specific base sequence, leaving short single-stranded "sticky ends". The same enzyme is used on the human DNA and the plasmid, so their sticky ends are complementary.
A small circle of bacterial DNA used as a vector. It has an origin of replication and a marker gene for antibiotic resistance.
Joins the sugar-phosphate backbones, sealing the gene into the plasmid: a recombinant plasmid.
Takes up the recombinant plasmid. Only bacteria with the plasmid survive on agar with the antibiotic (the marker).

g.text: agar with antibiotic: only transformed bacteria grow

g.data-info: Bacteria multiply in fermenters; every cell expresses the human gene and makes human insulin, which is purified for people with diabetes.
